newsitem.title: USA: USWeb says Utopia joins, expands network 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: USWeb says Utopia joins, expands network 25 pct.

text.p: USWeb Corp said it expects to announce on Tuesday that Utopia Inc will join its network of affiliates, expanding by 25 percent the domestic geographical reach of the Internet services firm.

"Two rivals have chosen to come together," said Joe Firmage, the founder and chief executive of USWeb, which aims to be the largest professional services company focused on the Internet's World Wide Web.

The deal with the Massachusetts-based Utopia, which was formed in 1992 and has rapidly growing Internet design, development and consulting business, raises the number of affiliate operated locations to 37 from 30, he said in an interview.

Utopia's offices serve customers in Boston, Chicago, Dallas/Fort Worth, New York, Orlando, the San Frandsco Bay Area, and Seattle. It will operate under the name USWeb Utopia, and has been granted territory expansion rights in Dallas/Fort Worth and most of the New England market.
"They represent, along with us, one of the top 10 Web presence companies in the nation," Firmage said.

"From their point of view looking at us, we have already established a national brand, we've already established a national infrastructure. They can take advantage of that rather than having to build it itself."

Firmage also said most of the operating affiliates in its network now serve major Fortune 500 companies, not simply the smaller businesses which some have thought would be its major focus of its franchise system.
"This drives a stake through the heart of the argument that USWeb is a small business-oriented company," he added.

Both are private companies. US Web received an investment of roughly $17 million from Softbank and its Ziff-Davis Publishing group and has venture backing from Crosspoint Venture Partners in nearby Los Altos, California.
